finding.claim: The weighted mean uses w_i = 1/sigma_i, which is not the inverse-variance (minimum-variance) weight.
finding.evidence_text: With w_i = 1/sigma_i^2 the mean is 10.0412; the stated 10.0493 follows from 1/sigma weights.

finding.claim: The efficiency uncertainty sqrt(k)/n treats k as Poisson and ignores that k and n are correlated (binomial).
The sample sizes are too small for a Gaussian approximation.
The uncertainty of the average should include a scale factor because the chi-square is large.

finding.claim: Something is off with the error propagation of P.
The relative uncertainty of P = A B omits the covariance term 2 rho rA rB; with rho = -0.7 the true uncertainty is smaller than stated.
finding.evidence_text: sqrt(rA^2 + rB^2 + 2 rho rA rB) gives 0.031 relative versus 0.058 stated.

finding.claim: Averaging with 1/sigma gives too much weight to imprecise measurements; the BLUE for independent inputs weights by inverse variance.
finding.evidence_text: Using 1/sigma^2 changes the mean by more than the 0.1% tolerance.
